answer: An atlas map gives each identity one vertex station. Claiming one locks 90 and files a key-bound ivory receipt per epoch. The atlas auditor burns the deposit for an empty station, a repeated receipt, or a shared vertex. Fees climb 8 per filled vertex, so a thousand fakes pay 4,038,000 plus 90,000 locked, dwarfing 40,000 reward. Rented slots fail: each ivory receipt fits its vertex. An honest agent pays 42 once, reclaims 90 after a clean epoch.
